analysis:
Reviewed the supplied base text of DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift (lines 1-778), plus the patch excerpt. The change is test-only. It renames the test aClusterServedThroughTheCoordinatorAsksForTheAssistantOnlyUnderAnExplicitOn to ...UnderAutoOnlyWhenDeclared. It adds a `declared` parameter to ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.discoveryMode(configured, coordinator:, declared:). It also adds tests, apparently an artifact-registered public-model check via ClusterPublicModels (head lines 791-834; the excerpt is truncated and head text was not supplied). No production code is in this batch, so no direct security regression is observable.

The test change implies a production behavior change that is not visible here. Under `auto`, a coordinator-served cluster now enables the tensor-parallel speculative assistant (MTP) when the build declares the assistant public for the artifact. Previously it was never enabled under `auto`. The security-relevant questions for the next pass are in the production sources, which I did not see:
- How `declared` is derived. It should come from a build-embedded registry keyed by the artifact digest, and not from provider-controlled config or the environment.
- Whether the coordinator-delivered setup actually carries the assistant, so there is no mismatch between provider and coordinator.
- Whether the assistant is still verified against the manifest and aggregate digest via automaticCandidate, which the existing tests exercise with a mismatched id or digest throwing.
- Whether the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_MTP=0 kill switch and the `off` mode are still respected.

Fixtures use constructed digests and hash("b") artifacts, with loopback and TEST-NET addresses, and no secrets. Related threat IDs: TB-007 and T-041 are tangentially affected only if the assistant changes cache or KV behavior, and T-027 if artifact identity binding weakens. I lack production evidence for any of these, so no finding is reported. A deeper review of the production discoveryMode and ClusterPublicModels is recommended.
